scheme_name: Providing Tin stalls to Gatai Kamgar
description:
The scheme for providing tin stalls to Gatai Kamgar is a significant initiative by the Government of India aimed at supporting marginalized workers in the unorganized sector. 

This scheme was launched on 1st January 2021. 

It was introduced to address the challenges faced by Gatai Kamgar, who are primarily involved in the preparation and sale of food items. 

The term "Gatai Kamgar" refers to workers who engage in the preparation of traditional Indian snacks and meals. 

These workers often operate in informal settings without proper infrastructure or facilities. 

The primary objective of the scheme is to provide these workers with a stable and secure environment to conduct their business. 

The government aims to enhance the livelihood opportunities for Gatai Kamgar by providing them with proper stalls. 

The scheme targets to provide around 50,000 tin stalls to eligible beneficiaries across various states in India. 

Each stall is designed to be durable and weather-resistant, ensuring that the workers can operate in various climatic conditions. 

The stalls are equipped with necessary features such as shelves for storage and a countertop for food preparation. 

The assistance provided under this scheme is valued at approximately ₹15,000 per stall. 

This amount is intended to cover the cost of materials and construction of the stalls. 

The scheme also aims to promote hygiene and safety in food preparation and sales. 

By providing a proper stall, the government seeks to reduce health risks associated with food preparation in unhygienic conditions. 

Eligibility for this scheme is primarily focused on Gatai Kamgar who are engaged in food preparation and sales. 

Applicants must be at least 18 years old to qualify for the scheme. 

There is no specific upper age limit for eligibility. 

Additionally, applicants must demonstrate that they are currently engaged in the Gatai Kamgar profession. 

Income criteria are set to ensure that the benefits reach the most marginalized workers. 

The annual income of the applicant must not exceed ₹2 lakh. 

This income limit is aimed at targeting low-income families who rely on this profession for their livelihood. 

The application process for the scheme is designed to be straightforward and accessible. 

Interested applicants must fill out an application form available at local government offices or online portals. 

The application form requires basic personal information such as name, age, address, and income details. 

Applicants must also provide proof of their engagement in the Gatai Kamgar profession. 

This can include affidavits or certificates from local authorities. 

Once the application is submitted, it is reviewed by the designated authorities. 

The review process typically takes about 30 days. 

Upon approval, the beneficiaries are notified through SMS or official communication. 

The disbursement of funds for the construction of the stalls occurs within two weeks of approval. 

The stalls are constructed by local contractors appointed by the government. 

The government ensures that the construction adheres to quality standards and safety regulations. 

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Ministry of Labour and Employment. 

State governments also play a crucial role in the execution of the scheme. 

They are responsible for identifying beneficiaries and overseeing the construction of the stalls. 

Contact details for the Ministry of Labour and Employment can be found on their official website. 

The scheme also aligns with the broader goals of the government to promote entrepreneurship among informal workers. 

By providing infrastructure, the government aims to empower Gatai Kamgar to expand their businesses. 

The initiative is part of a larger framework of welfare schemes aimed at improving the livelihoods of informal sector workers. 

The government has allocated a budget of ₹75 crore for the implementation of this scheme in the first year. 

This budget is expected to cover the costs of stall construction and administrative expenses. 

The scheme is expected to benefit not only the Gatai Kamgar but also the local economy. 

By formalizing their operations, these workers can potentially increase their earnings. 

The government also plans to provide training programs for Gatai Kamgar to enhance their skills. 

These training programs will focus on food safety, hygiene, and business management. 

The training is expected to be rolled out in collaboration with local NGOs and training institutes. 

The scheme is part of the government's ongoing efforts to uplift the informal sector. 

It aims to provide social security and financial stability to workers who often lack these benefits. 

The government encourages local communities to support Gatai Kamgar by purchasing from their stalls. 

This initiative is expected to foster a sense of community and support local businesses. 

The scheme has received positive feedback from various stakeholders. 

Local governments have reported an increase in the number of applications since the launch. 

The initiative is seen as a step towards recognizing the contributions of informal workers. 

It aims to provide them with dignity and respect in their profession. 

The government is committed to monitoring the progress of the scheme. 

Regular assessments will be conducted to evaluate its impact on the livelihoods of Gatai Kamgar. 

The scheme is expected to evolve based on feedback from beneficiaries and local authorities. 

In conclusion, the provision of tin stalls to Gatai Kamgar is a crucial welfare initiative. 

It aims to empower informal workers by providing them with the necessary infrastructure to thrive. 

The scheme not only supports individual livelihoods but also contributes to the overall economic development of the community. 

The government remains dedicated to enhancing the welfare of Gatai Kamgar through this and other related initiatives. 

This scheme represents a significant investment in the future of informal workers in India. 

It is a testament to the government's commitment to social justice and economic empowerment.
